workingTitle: JWST detects a forbidden molecular fingerprint for the first time
publicationStatus: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters; arXiv v1 listed November 10, 2026
coreFacts: JWST/MIRI detected 26 uncontaminated forbidden rotational lines of H3+ above five sigma in at least one of two HH 168 fields.
The strongest line at 16.325 micrometres was detected at 72 sigma in field G and 49 sigma in field C.
The H3+ emission shares the velocity and spatial distribution of hot shocked molecular hydrogen rather than ionized gas.
A rotation diagram gives about 730 kelvin, but subthermal populations imply collisions in gas hotter than about 2000 kelvin.
J-type shock models reproduce the H3+ emission within about a factor of 1.5 but exceed the shock code's validated range; C-type models underpredict it by factors of five to six.
Archival JWST data independently show the same spectrum in the HH 211 bow shock.

sources.label: Neufeld et al. accepted ApJ Letters paper

sourceStatus: Full primary paper and arXiv metadata read; primary source directly supports all material claims.
caveats: High-energy H3+-H2 collision rates are poorly known.
The preferred J-type shock model lies outside the validated range of the shock code.
The lines are a new ionization probe, but quantitative interpretation requires better collision data.
